name: Coating aged (oil paint, lacquer, ground)
describes: Chenghuai's painted and lacquered timber ages from the top down. UV and weather break down the oil and lacquer binders at the surface: gloss falls, the surface chalks and lightens, and a fine craze (断纹) opens as the film embrittles and the timber moves beneath it. Where cracks let water into the ground, the 地仗 loosens and flakes, showing grey ground and hemp. Mineral pigments (iron-oxide red) hold their hue; the binder around them goes. Under eaves and on rafters, soot and dust darken the red.

cracks.text: SEM showed cracks: iron formulations a flat surface with linear cracks, carbon black formulations wrinkles and cracks.

rhCycling.text: Micro-cracking after RH cycling occurred on most lacquer samples, in many patterns; transparent lacquers retained the highest gloss and showed the least micro-cracking.
rhCycling.source: Webb, M. (2016) A new understanding of the aging characteristics of Asian lacquer. AIC Objects Specialty Group Postprints 23, https://resources.culturalheritage.org/osg-postprints/v23/webb/ (abstract read)

oilBinder.text: 光油 (广油) has the poorest ageing resistance of the transparent finishes.
oilBinder.source: 雅昌艺术市场监测中心 (2018) 明清家具透明涂料的成分与鉴别 [The composition and identification of the clear finishes of Ming and Qing furniture], 2018-10-10, https://amma.artron.net/observation_shownews.php?newid=1030835

pigment.text: Mineral pigments are in the low light-sensitivity class.
pigment.source: Michalski, S. (2018) Agent of deterioration: light, ultraviolet and infrared. Canadian Conservation Institute, 2018-05-17, https://www.canada.ca/en/conservation-institute/services/agents-deterioration/light.html

terms.craze: 断纹: a network of cells a few millimetres to a couple of centimetres across on old lacquer and paint; its scale is to be measured (see unverified).

bySubstance.korean-pine: Columns and frames: checks along the grain through the red; chalking on sunlit faces; flaking at the foot where splashed.
bySubstance.chinese-fir: Rafters and boards: darkened by smoke and dust; flaking at the eaves.

up: sky exposure and sun (Form's piece facts, the Moment)

photograph: Old red columns: dull, slightly pink-chalky on the sun side, a fine crackle, flakes missing near the base; deep and glossy in the shade.
Garden lacquer: gloss lost on sunlit rails, intact under the roof.

evidence.shows: A crack network from a dried riverbed's relief, rescaled to 0.3 m to stand for lacquer craze (the first build described cells 5-20 mm, cracks 0.1-0.3 mm). Pattern only; not a photograph of lacquer.

roughnessMapMedian.derivation: green channel of ORM.png, 256 x 256 bilinear resample; median, with percentiles 5/50/95 in the note
roughnessMapMedian.note: authored roughness map, not a measurement; percentiles 5/50/95 = 0.333/0.427/0.525

unverified.reason: The first build's 5-20 mm cells and 0.1-0.3 mm cracks are its own description, not a measurement.
The interval at which Qing official buildings were repainted was not read.
